statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 3. Let X be a terminal, Q-factorial projective threefold, let (X, B) be log canonical with rational boundary, and let 0 ̸= N0 ∼ m(KX + B) be an effective nef Cartier divisor, where m is a positive integer. Assume that N0 is numerically trivial on each component of its support, and that every component of B is either contained in or disjoint from Supp N0. Denote by Pout the union of the latter components and put UX = Xreg \ Supp N0 ∪ Pout  . There exist a projective Q-factorial klt threefold Y birational to X, a rational boundary GY , an effective nef Q-Cartier divisor NY , and a prime divisor SY with the following properties. 1. The pair (Y, GY ) is log canonical, SY has coefficient one in GY , and s := multSY NY is positive. For rational numbers τ > 0 and δ > 0, KY + GY ∼Q τNY , KY + GY − δSY is nef. (8) 2. The divisor NY is numerically trivial on every component of its support. Every component of GY is either contained in or disjoint from Supp NY . 3. The divisor SY is disjoint from every other component of NY and from Supp(GY − SY ). In particular, NY = sSY , GY = SY , KY + SY ∼Q τsSY (9) on a neighborhood of SY , and SY |SY ≡ 0. 4. The birational correspondence identifies UX with an open subset of Y . On a smooth projective common resolution q : V0 → X, r : V0 → Y that is an isomorphism over this open, q∗ N0 = r∗ NY . (10) The same equality holds after passing to any further common resolution. One may take τ = m−1 + λ, where λ = lct(X,B)(N0) ≥ 0.
